title: A caliper boxed in by two full-width rows finds a better home for its number than straddling them
goal: When you measure the space between two rows that run the full width of the picture, the number has nowhere clear within reach and stays on the line, covering a bit of both rows. Decide with the user what the better last resort is, for example tucking it in the page margin or past the rows on a longer connector.
notes: Comes from queue/audits/2026-09-02-caliper-subjects.json rough item 1. MeasureLabelPlanner.maxCrossReach caps sideways travel at three chip heights; the boxed-in fallback is the flat subjectPenalty tie-break to .onLine. Same limit shows up for Size mode on a full-width row (2026-08-23-size-readout-placement rough item 1). Render scripts: temp/boxed-in/Scan.swift (sweep) and temp/boxed-in/Render.swift (four options); compile with swiftc -I .build/debug/Modules against .build/debug/PhotonzCore.build/*.o and PhotonzRender.build/*.o. Option renders live in queue/audits/2026-09-02-boxed-in-*.png.
acceptance: A decision card offers the user two or three visible options for the boxed-in case with rendered examples on the audit capture.
The chosen option is implemented in Next and the callout clearance sweep covers it.

Reproduced on the audit capture: a sweep of every Gap-mode gap (temp/boxed-in/Scan.swift, 931 gaps) finds three boxed-in placements, all vertical: the 33 px space between the two cards (y 417-450) where the 44 px pill overhangs both cards, and the two row heights measured between dividers (y 236-321, y 540-625) where the pill sits inside the row it measures, which is fine.

Adversarial review of the idea: the overhang is a few pixels per side at the picture scale and the feet stay visible, so the problem is smaller than the audit line suggested. The margin option fails on this capture outright (64 px margin, 93 px pill). Past-the-foot reads as the row's number. Shrink is the only option that keeps the number unmistakably at the gap, at the price of mixed pill sizes.
Rendered all four options through DocumentRenderer (temp/boxed-in/Render.swift): queue/audits/2026-09-02-boxed-in-{a-straddle,b-past-foot,c-shrink,d-margin}.png.

Opened decision a-caliper-boxed-in-by-two-full-width-rows-finds-when-a-gap-caliper-sits-between with brief; recommended straddle (keep today). If straddle wins, the implementation is to pin it in MeasureCalloutClearanceTests (the gap sweep already tolerates boxed-in) and close.

Side find, filed as a-gap-caliper-whose-foot-lands-under-a-row-label (p2): at x=330 the upper row is not returned as a subject and the planner nudges the pill up onto the "Play sound on capture" label.
Waiting on the decision: where the number goes when two full-width rows box the caliper in. Four options rendered on the audit capture; straddle (today) recommended.
decision "When a gap caliper sits between two full-width rows and its number cannot fit anywhere clear, where should the number go?" resolved: Stay on the line, straddling both rows

Adversarial review of the chosen answer before pinning it: straddle is what the code already does, so the risk is not building the wrong thing, it is that nobody knows it was chosen. Re-ran the sweep on the audit capture: 147 boxed-in placements across 338 gaps, every one centred on the line. The overhang the user accepted is real and small at the user's own label size (chip 93x47 on the 33 px card gap): 1.5 px onto the upper card, 5.5 px onto the lower one, both caliper feet uncovered.

Checked the neighbouring behaviour so the pin does not over-claim: near either margin (x 200, x 1200) the number is NOT boxed in, it takes the long leash out to the page margin. That is the separately resolved travel decision (keep the long leash), not this one, so the pin only covers gaps with nothing clear in reach.

Pinned it: MeasureCalloutClearanceTests gains aCaliperBoxedInByTwoFullWidthRowsKeepsItsNumberAtTheGap (x 700 and x 1000, asserts the case really is boxed in, the plan is exactly onLine/0/0, the chip is centred on the gap, off the caliper, and dips no more than 8 px into either card) and everyBoxedInCaliperOnTheCaptureKeepsTheClassicSpot (every boxed-in gap on the capture, all three heads). The gap list is now one shared static so both sweeps judge the same population.

Mutation-checked the pin: making subjectPenalty count subjects instead of being flat sends the number two nudge steps down into the lower card, and all three tests fail (plus the existing core-level aBoxedInCaliperKeepsTheClassicSpot). Reverted; the flat penalty is unchanged.
Recorded the choice at the source: MeasureLabelPlanner.subjectPenalty now documents that the flat cost is the user's answer, not a shortcut, and that weighting it by count or depth un-picks it.

No user-visible change, so no audit was written: the chosen option is today's behaviour. Re-rendered the straddle for the record (temp/boxed-in/cards-a-straddle.png) and eyeballed it, the number reads as the gap's and both card edges stay legible. Scripts/test.sh green, 1449 tests.

The user's answer (stay on the line, straddling both rows) is now pinned rather than emergent: MeasureCalloutClearanceTests gets aCaliperBoxedInByTwoFullWidthRowsKeepsItsNumberAtTheGap and everyBoxedInCaliperOnTheCaptureKeepsTheClassicSpot (147 boxed-in placements on the audit capture, all centred), and MeasureLabelPlanner.subjectPenalty documents why it is flat. No behaviour change; verified by re-planning every gap before and after, by mutating the penalty (all three tests fail), and by eyeballing a fresh render. Scripts/test.sh green, 1449 tests.
